items.prompt: Where do rocks come from?

figure.alt: A rock and a rocky mountain.

options.why: Rocks are natural. People do not make them in factories.
Trees give us wood. Rocks are found in the ground.
Rocks are part of the Earth's land, under our feet.

hints: Think about where you find stones when you dig.
Ask: what is under the soil if you dig deep?
items.explanation: Rocks come from the ground. They are a natural material, and the Earth's land is made of rock under the soil.

items.prompt: Choose all the things made from rock or stone.

options.why: A wooden door is made from trees.

hints: Rock and stone are hard natural materials.
Gravel is made of many small stones.
Start with the stone wall. What is it made of?
items.explanation: Stone walls, stone statues and gravel paths are made from rock. A wooden door comes from trees and a woollen hat comes from sheep.

items.prompt: What is sand made of?

figure.alt: A pile of sand with tiny grains.

options.why: Sand is not food. It is made of tiny bits of rock.
People make glass from sand. Sand itself is natural.

hints: Look closely at sand with a magnifying glass.
Each grain is hard, like a very tiny stone.
Ask: what happens to rocks after many years of wind and waves?
items.explanation: Sand is made of tiny bits of rock, and sometimes bits of shell. Wind and water break rocks into tiny grains over a very long time.

items.prompt: Which things are natural parts of soil? Sort the cards.
hints: Soil forms in nature over a long time.
Ask: did people make it and leave it there?
Start with the tiny bits of rock. Where did they come from?
items.explanation: Soil is made of tiny bits of rock, bits of dead plants and animals, water and air. Plastic, glass and cans are litter that people leave behind.

items.prompt: Plants grow in ___. It has tiny bits of rock, water and air in it.

figure.alt: A young plant growing in brown ground, marked with a question mark.

hints: Think about what you fill a plant pot with.
It is brown and you can dig in it.
items.explanation: Plants grow in soil. Soil has tiny bits of rock, bits of dead plants, water and air in it.

items.prompt: Which animal lives in soil and helps keep it healthy?

options.why: Polar bears live in the icy Arctic.
Eagles live in the sky and in tall trees.

hints: Think about digging in a garden after rain.
Which animal wriggles under the ground?
Its name has the word earth in it.
items.explanation: Earthworms live in soil. They make tunnels that let in air and water, and they help dead leaves rot into the soil.

items.prompt: Borobudur temple is built from stone. Why is stone a good material for it?

options.text: It is hard and lasts a very long time.
It goes soft in the rain.
options.why: Stone stays hard in the rain.

hints: Think about how old Borobudur is.
A building must stand up and last.
Ask: which property helps something last hundreds of years?
items.explanation: Stone is hard and strong and lasts a very long time. Borobudur was built about 1,200 years ago and is still standing.

items.prompt: Rocks in a river are often round and smooth. Why?

figure.alt: A river with round, smooth pebbles.

options.why: Rivers do this on their own, without people.

options.text: Water rubs them for a very long time.

options.why: The Sun is not hot enough to melt rocks.

hints: Think about what moves over river rocks all day.
Rocks also knock against each other in the water.
Ask: what happens to sharp corners that are rubbed for years?
items.explanation: River water and other stones rub against the rocks for a very long time. Their sharp corners wear away, so they become round and smooth.

items.prompt: Hot lava comes out of a volcano. What happens when it cools?

figure.alt: A volcano with hot lava flowing down its side.

options.why: Lava is melted rock. It does not become water.
The lava is still there. It changes.

options.text: It turns into sand straight away.
options.why: Cooled lava becomes solid rock. Rock can break into sand over a very long time.

hints: Lava is rock that is so hot it has melted.
Think about what happens to melted chocolate when it cools.
Ask: if hot melted rock cools, what is it again?
items.explanation: Lava is melted rock. When it cools down, it turns into hard, solid rock.

items.prompt: Farmers near volcanoes in Java often grow good crops. Why?

options.why: Rain waters the crops. Volcanoes do not.

options.text: Soil made from volcanic ash is very good for plants.

options.why: The crops grow well because of the soil.
Plants do not eat rocks. Their roots take in water and some goodness from the soil.

hints: Think about what falls on the land after an eruption.
Over many years, volcanic ash becomes part of the soil.
Ask: what do plant roots grow in?
items.explanation: Volcanic ash slowly becomes rich soil. Plants grow well in it, so farmers near volcanoes often have good crops.

items.prompt: Joko pours 100 ml of water onto some sand. The jug shows the water that drained through. How much drained through?

figure.alt: A jug with 80 ml of water in it.

hints: Look at the top of the water in the jug.
Each mark on the jug is 10 ml.
Count up the marks from the bottom to the water.
items.explanation: The water reaches the 80 ml mark, so 80 ml drained through the sand. Sand lets water through easily.

items.prompt: Which one lets water through most easily?

figure.caption: Water that drained through in 1 minute
head: Soil
Water through
figure.alt: Table of water that drained through in 1 minute: sand 80 ml, garden soil 50 ml, clay 10 ml.

options.why: Only 50 ml went through garden soil. Sand let more through.
Only 10 ml went through clay. It holds water back.
The numbers are different, so they are not the same.

hints: Look at the water through column.
The most water means the easiest path for water.
Find the biggest number in the table.
items.explanation: 80 ml went through the sand, which is the most. Sand has big gaps between its grains, so water drains through easily.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
pairs: rock bits mixed with dead plants, water and air
hints: Read every meaning before you match.
Do the one you are sure of first.
Start with lava. Where does it come from?
items.explanation: Sand is tiny grains of rock and a pebble is a small, smooth stone. Soil is rock bits mixed with dead plants, water and air, and lava is melted rock from a volcano.

items.prompt: How do earthworms help plants grow?

figure.alt: An earthworm making a tunnel in the soil.

options.why: Earthworms eat dead leaves and bits in the soil.
Worms make soil softer and looser.

options.text: Their tunnels let air and water into the soil.

hints: Think about what worms do all day under the ground.
Roots need air and water in the soil.
Ask: what do worm tunnels let in?
items.explanation: Earthworms dig tunnels that let air and water reach the roots. They also help dead leaves rot into the soil.

items.prompt: The school wants a path for the rainy season. It must not get muddy. Which material is best?

options.why: Soil turns to mud when it rains.
Clay gets sticky and slippery when it is wet.
Paper goes soggy and tears in the rain.

hints: Rain must drain away quickly on a good path.
Small stones have gaps between them.
Ask: which one stays firm when it is wet?
items.explanation: Gravel is made of small stones with gaps between them. Rainwater drains away, so a gravel path stays firm and does not turn to mud.

items.prompt: Draw a slice of the ground. Show soil on top and rock below. Add a worm and some roots.

criteria.label: Draws soil on top and rock underneath
Draws a worm in the soil
Draws plant roots growing down into the soil
Labels the soil and the rock

hints: Draw a line across the page for the top of the ground.
Put the rock at the bottom of your picture.
items.explanation: Soil is on top, with roots and worms in it. Under the soil is solid rock.

items.prompt: Wayan digs a deep hole and writes what he sees. Which layer has the most bits of dead plants?

head: Layer
What it looks like
rows: dark brown, with bits of leaves and roots
figure.alt: Table of soil layers. Top: dark brown, with bits of leaves and roots. Middle: lighter brown, with small stones. Bottom: hard rock.

options.why: The middle layer has small stones and fewer bits of leaves.
The bottom layer is hard rock.
The layers look different from each other.

hints: Read what each layer looks like.
Dead leaves fall on top of the ground and rot there.
Look for the words leaves and roots in the table.
items.explanation: The top layer has bits of leaves and roots, which makes it dark brown. Leaves fall and rot on top, so the top layer has the most dead plant bits.

items.prompt: Which one is a kind of rock?
hints: It is hard and often shiny.
items.explanation: Marble is a rock. People use it for floors and statues.

items.prompt: Which word describes most rocks?
items.explanation: Most rocks are hard.

items.prompt: What is the top layer of the ground, where plants grow?

options.why: Metal is not in the top layer.

items.explanation: Plants grow in soil.

items.prompt: Which rock can we use to write on a board?
items.explanation: Chalk is a soft rock. It leaves white marks on a board.

items.prompt: Why are rocks useful?

options.text: We use them to build houses and roads.

items.explanation: Rocks such as granite and stone are hard and strong. We use them for buildings and roads.

items.prompt: Which soil holds water the best?
items.explanation: Clay soil has tiny pieces, so water stays in it. Sandy soil lets water run through.

items.prompt: How does sandy soil feel?
hints: It is the opposite of smooth.
items.explanation: Sandy soil has bigger bits that feel gritty.

items.prompt: A farmer wants soil that gives plants plenty of food. Which is best?

options.text: soil with lots of big stones
soil with lots of rotted leaves

hints: Plants need food from the soil.
items.explanation: Rotted leaves add food to the soil. This helps plants grow well.

items.prompt: Are the pieces big or tiny? Sort the cards.
items.explanation: Boulders, pebbles and stones are big pieces. Sand, clay and mud are tiny pieces.

items.prompt: Natural rock or made from rock? Sort the cards.
items.explanation: Granite, pebbles and marble blocks are natural rock. Bricks are made from clay, concrete from stone and sand, and glass from sand.

items.prompt: Choose all the things found in soil.
items.explanation: Soil has tiny bits of rock, air, water and dead plants. Bottles and wires are rubbish and are not part of soil.

items.prompt: Choose all the animals that live in soil.
items.explanation: Worms, ants and beetles live in soil. Ducks live on ponds and sharks live in the sea.

items.prompt: Match each rock to how we use it.
hints: Slate splits into thin flat pieces.
items.explanation: We carve statues from marble and use granite for kitchen tops. Slate makes roof tiles and chalk is for writing.

items.prompt: Put the steps in order to test how soil drains.
items: pour 100 ml of water on top
measure the water in the jug
items.explanation: Put soil in the funnel and pour water on top. Wait, then measure the water that drained into the jug.

items.prompt: Soil is made of tiny bits of ___, dead plants and air.
items.explanation: Soil has tiny bits of rock, dead plants, air and water.

items.prompt: Pour 100 ml of water on each soil. How much does each soil hold?
head: Soil
Drained (ml)
Held (ml)
items.explanation: The soil holds the water that does not drain. Clay holds 100 - 20 = 80 ml. Garden soil holds 100 - 50 = 50 ml.

items.prompt: Kai and Lia dig up two soils. The sandy soil is pale and gritty. The clay soil is dark and sticky. They pour water on both. The water goes through the sand quickly. It stays on top of the clay.

parts.prompt: Which soil lets water through quickly?
How does the clay soil feel?

items.explanation: Water goes through sandy soil quickly. The clay soil is sticky.

items.prompt: Mei pours 100 ml of water onto sand. 70 ml drains into the jug. How many ml stay in the sand?
hints: Take away the water in the jug.
items.explanation: 100 - 70 = 30. Thirty ml stay in the sand.

items.prompt: Tap the rock.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: rock, feather, leaf and cup.

items.explanation: A rock is a hard, natural object.

items.prompt: Tap the soil.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: soil, sand, water and feather.

items.explanation: Soil is the dark layer where plants grow.

items.prompt: A soft white rock that can write on a board is ___.
items.explanation: Chalk is a soft rock. We use it to write on boards.

items.prompt: Rock X scratches rock Y. Rock Y scratches rock Z. Which rock is the hardest?

options.why: Rock Z is scratched by Y.

items.explanation: A harder rock scratches a softer rock. X scratches Y and Y scratches Z, so X is hardest.

items.prompt: Water is poured on three soils. A holds 20 ml. B holds 50 ml. C holds 80 ml. Which drains fastest?
items.explanation: Soil A holds the least water, so most of the water runs through it.

items.prompt: A plant pot has holes in the bottom. Why?

options.text: So the plant can see out.

items.explanation: Holes let extra water drain away so the roots do not sit in water.
